frozen_before: Any A1 shared-candidate evaluation on the dev set (identity dev runs are allowed before freezing: they are candidate-independent).

dev_set.role: configuration screening only; not a quality certification set

candidates.construction: Frozen v28 R0 checkpoint (R4-trained weights, native_policy.blocks=0). G20/G24 keep a subset of consumers via sharedkv_v21.bundles.isolate(bundle, kept_consumers); reverted consumers read their own prefix KV. No reader value changes, no retraining, no new sources. validate_sources (one-hop, same P8 window, leaders native) must pass.
candidates.revert_order_rule: Label-free, fixed before evaluation: sort consumers by descending |l - s(l)|, ties by ascending layer index. G20 reverts the first 4, G24 the first 8.
candidates.not_monotonic_warning: Reverting consumers changes downstream hidden states and online P8 selections; every candidate is evaluated end to end.

eligibility.metric: paired net correct-count difference on the same dev queries: correct(candidate) - correct(I)
eligibility.threshold: correct(candidate) - correct(I) >= -ceil(0.01 * n); for n = 500 at most 5 net fewer correct answers. Integer counts only; no rounded percentages.

selection.bytes_definition: Mean over requests of physical_prefetch_kv_bytes = _physical_tokens x bytes_per_token (K+V), where _physical_tokens accumulates, in flexgen_pcache._resolve_entry/_record_physical_access, the physical prefix token ids resolved for every physically resolved source layer of the first Re-Prefill, from ANY tier (GPU hit, CPU, disk). Verified: for I it equals selected_kv_bytes exactly (sst2_b5: 10,550,380 B), so label-continuation scoring adds nothing; quality runs use warmup 0. Excludes selector index, reader/packed weights, private query/generation KV, and device-level I/O. Not a minimum-total-memory or hardware H2D measure; source count, reader/packed resident bytes and net working set are reported separately.
selection.missing_bytes: a candidate whose bytes field is missing or non-finite is invalid for selection; never treated as 0; pause and revise
selection.tie_rule: Let B_min be the smallest bytes among eligible candidates. Among eligible candidates with (B - B_min) / B_min < 0.005 choose, in order: larger net correct-count difference; fewer shared consumers; fixed name order I, G24, G20, G16, then any A2 candidate by name.
selection.no_eligible_shared: Select I and report the cell as having no qualified compression point.
recorded_not_used: mean KL between candidate-label score distributions (softmax over mean label log-prob, T=1) vs I

data_size_pilot.data: fit512: 512 new queries per task, disjoint from dev and all historical roles, built with the dev-set exclusion rule (seed 2902). fit64: the first 64 of fit512 in the frozen shuffled order, so fit64 is a subset of fit512 and both arms have identical historical exposure.
data_size_pilot.initialization: Both arms use the compiler default initialization (initial=None, sharedkv_v24.train.initialize): per KV head, affine ridge regression (ridge=0.001) mapping the source layer's cached prefix K/V to the consumer layer's cached prefix K/V, read from the prefix store (read_prefix). It uses no fit/val/dev queries, so fit64 and fit512 start from an identical initialization that has not seen the new data. Same seed (24) for both arms.
data_size_pilot.fixed: same source map (G16), seed, validation set (existing v26 val traces), optimizer, loss, checkpoint-selection rule; both arms perform exactly 512 query updates (fit64: 8 passes, fit512: 1 pass); train with R4, infer with frozen R0
data_size_pilot.sampling: rev 2: epoch-shuffled sampling WITHOUT replacement for both arms (the legacy trainer samples with replacement via rng.randrange, which would cover only ~63% of fit512 in 512 steps). Implemented by scripts/train_v29_epoch.py, which replaces random.Random in sharedkv_v24.train with a seeded epoch-permutation generator; legacy code unchanged. Each pass is a fresh seeded permutation; fit64 = exactly 8 passes, fit512 = exactly 1 pass.
data_size_pilot.teacher: teacher records captured with the same identity capture command as v26 (collect_teacher_v26.py, budget of the cell, P8), separately for fit64 and fit512; plan = v26 cell plan sources with design_query_hashes = the arm's own fit hashes
data_size_pilot.switch: Engineering switch, not a significance claim: enable recalibration only if correct(fit512) - correct(fit64) >= ceil(0.01 * n) (>= 5 of 500) on the dev set, R0 inference, in BOTH pilot cells. Compared arm vs arm under identical training conditions; not vs the old 200-step checkpoint and not only vs I.
data_size_pilot.pilot_results_are_candidates: The pilot fit512 checkpoints (and fit64) are A2 candidates for their cells and go through the same eligibility/selection rule; they are not retrained if the switch fires.

recalibration.trigger: cell (other than the two pilots) whose selected configuration after A1 is I or G24
recalibration.recipe: G16 structure retrained with the fit512 recipe, only if the pilot switch fired; otherwise no recalibration
recalibration.same_rule: each A2 candidate is judged once by this eligibility/selection rule; no further tuning on dev

freeze_after_a2: Record final configuration and checkpoint SHA-256 per cell, then rerun full 16-cell test-set quality for the selected configurations (plus I) before any timing. Old G16 accuracy is never paired with a different configuration's TTFT.

timing_design.arms: I, G16 (frozen v28 R0), and the selected configuration if its checkpoint or execution config differs from both; a retrained G16 is a different arm from the frozen G16

ordinary_cache.cells: 4 tasks x {25%, 50%} = 8 cells, fixed in advance by budget, not by results

timing_design.order: each block runs all arms; 6 blocks cover all 6 orders of 3 arms (Latin/complete balance); 2 arms alternate
timing_design.analysis: paired by block; report per-block direction; no significance guarantee from 6 blocks

timing_telemetry.exclusive: GPU2, cores 28-31,60-63; no other job of this user anywhere on the host
pre_start_gate: nvidia-smi: no compute process on GPU2 or GPU3
timing cores 28-31,60-63 TOTAL busy < 1 core averaged over 30 s (/proc/stat)
sda TOTAL read+write < 5 MB/s over 30 s (/proc/diskstats)
timing_telemetry.recorded_not_gated: total busy on background CPUs 0-11,16-27 and the rest of NUMA1 (to document the load level)
timing_telemetry.in_run_sampling: every 5 s: nvidia-smi compute processes per GPU; per-process CPU time deltas from /proc/<pid>/stat for every process (attributable: owner, pid, cpus_allowed); /proc/<pid>/io for processes of this user; totals from /proc/stat and /proc/diskstats recorded but not used for attribution
timing_telemetry.block_flag: attributable evidence only: a foreign compute process on GPU2/GPU3, or processes outside the timing process tree last run on the timing cores using >= 1 core over any 30 s window
timing_telemetry.flagged_block: keep and mark; rerun the whole paired block (all arms, same queries, same order) once; if the rerun is also flagged, report both and mark the cell interfered
timing_telemetry.never: drop or rerun blocks based on observed TTFT

change_control.semantic: changes to candidates, thresholds, byte definition, missing-field handling, data membership or validity: pause affected parts, keep the old rule, publish a new revision number and SHA-256, rerun every affected comparison under one rule (never only the unfavorable arm)
change_control.non_semantic: path fixes, extra logging, equivalent parsing fixes: record code diff and passing tests, continue; unaffected results are not rerun

reporting.main_table: accuracy and change vs I per cell; Full-KV per task listed as a reference (never called an upper bound)
reporting.companion_table: disagreement rate and label-score KL vs I
reporting.wording: Task accuracy measures answer quality; disagreement and KL measure fidelity to the no-sharing sparse system; the two can diverge (applies to all tasks). SUBJ/25% is highly sensitive to the selection reuse period: on the dev set, P4 recovers no-sharing accuracy (P8 57.4, P4 85.0, P1 86.8); only 25% was tested.

timing_environment.background_load: Unauthorized persistent process (/tmp/mysqld, 24 threads each pinned to one CPU: 0-11 and 16-27) present on the host, respawned via a PAM hook on every login/sudo/cron session. The user decided on 2026-09-29 to measure without cleanup. Historical timings (prism_pans rounds, v26-v28) were very likely taken under the same load. Absolute TTFT is therefore host-condition specific; comparisons are paired within blocks under identical conditions.
timing_environment.cores: 28-31,60-63: the 4 NUMA1 physical cores (plus HT siblings) not used by the background threads; all arms identical
